title: Gutenberg prints the Bible with movable type

when.label: c. 1454–1455
when.note: The Library of Congress dates the printing to 1454/1455 and says it was probably completed late in 1455.

where.name: Mainz
where.note: Marker placed at the centre of Mainz; the exact workshop location is not shown.

summary: In Mainz, Johannes Gutenberg and his partner Johann Fust produced the first great book printed in Europe with movable metal type.
description: Johannes Gutenberg, who lived from about 1400 to about 1468, is generally credited with inventing a process for making uniform, interchangeable metal type. With his partner Johann Fust he printed a Latin Bible in Mainz; the printing was probably completed late in 1455.
The print run may have been as many as 180 copies, about a quarter of them on vellum rather than paper.
context: The first written reference to printing in Europe dates to 1455, when Aeneas Silvius Piccolomini, secretary to the Holy Roman Emperor Frederick III, wrote to a cardinal in Rome about a man he had met with bibles for sale. The Library of Congress describes the Gutenberg Bible as a turning point in the art of bookmaking.

facts.text: The Bible was printed in Mainz in 1454/1455 by Gutenberg and Fust.
Perhaps as many as 180 copies were printed.

uncertain.text: The exact dates of Gutenberg's life and of the printing are not documented precisely; the Library of Congress gives 'about 1400 to about 1468' for his life.
